database_summary: Transactional e-commerce dataset (SQLite) containing customers, sellers, orders and related event/detail tables (order_items, order_payments, order_reviews), product catalog and translations, and geolocation lookups. Tables include identifiers that link orders -> customers, order_items -> orders & sellers & products, order_payments -> orders, order_reviews -> orders, products -> product_id, geolocation keyed by zip prefix. Mix of current state (customers, sellers, products) and event/history rows (orders, order_items, order_payments, order_reviews).

accepted.name: orders_enriched_times
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  customer_id,
  order_status,
  order_purchase_timestamp,
  order_approved_at,
  order_delivered_carrier_date,
  order_delivered_customer_date,
  order_estimated_delivery_date,
  -- parsed as ISO8601 text (SQLite will accept original if already ISO-like); keep originals too
  CASE WHEN order_purchase_timestamp = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_purchase_timestamp END AS order_purchase_timestamp_normalized,
  CASE WHEN order_approved_at = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_approved_at END AS order_approved_at_normalized,
  CASE WHEN order_delivered_carrier_date = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_delivered_carrier_date END AS order_delivered_carrier_date_normalized,
  CASE WHEN order_delivered_customer_date = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_delivered_customer_date END AS order_delivered_customer_date_normalized,
  CASE WHEN order_estimated_delivery_date = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_estimated_delivery_date END AS order_estimated_delivery_date_normalized,
  -- derived: delivery latency in seconds where timestamps available (NULL-safe)
  CASE
    WHEN order_approved_at IS NOT NULL AND order_purchase_timestamp IS NOT NULL AND order_approved_at <> '' AND order_purchase_timestamp <> ''
    THEN (strftime('%s', order_approved_at) - strftime('%s', order_purchase_timestamp))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS approval_lag_seconds,
  CASE
    WHEN order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL AND order_purchase_timestamp IS NOT NULL AND order_delivered_customer_date <> '' AND order_purchase_timestamp <> ''
    THEN (strftime('%s', order_delivered_customer_date) - strftime('%s', order_purchase_timestamp))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS purchase_to_delivery_seconds,
  CASE
    WHEN order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL AND order_estimated_delivery_date IS NOT NULL AND order_delivered_customer_date <> '' AND order_estimated_delivery_date <> ''
    THEN (strftime('%s', order_delivered_customer_date) - strftime('%s', order_estimated_delivery_date))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS delivery_vs_estimate_seconds
FROM orders
accepted.description: Normalize orders timestamps into ISO8601 and expose delivery lag measures. Use when analyzing time-to-approve / time-to-deliver metrics or joining orders by normalized timestamps. | Use for: Calculate average time-to-approve orders; Compute delivery lateness vs estimate; Filter orders by purchase or delivery time windows; Correlate delivery speed with review scores or customer attributes

accepted.name: order_items_financials
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  order_item_id,
  product_id,
  seller_id,
  shipping_limit_date,
  price,
  freight_value,
  -- derived total charged for the item
  (COALESCE(price, 0.0) + COALESCE(freight_value, 0.0)) AS item_total_value
FROM order_items
accepted.description: Clean and expose per-order-item financials (price, freight, and total). Use as the canonical per-item monetary row for aggregations or joins to products/sellers/orders. | Use for: Aggregate sales or freight by order or seller; Find most valuable items or orders by sum of item_total_value; Compute average item price or freight by product category or seller

accepted.name: order_payments_agg_by_order
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  COUNT(*) AS payment_attempts_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(payment_value, 0.0)) AS payment_total_value,
  MIN(payment_type) AS any_payment_type_sample,
  MAX(payment_installments) AS max_payment_installments
FROM order_payments
GROUP BY order_id
accepted.description: Aggregate payments to the order level: total paid, number of installments records, and count of payment attempts. Use when comparing paid value to order item totals or computing payment-method mixes per order. | Use for: Compare paid amount to order items total; Segment orders by payment type or installment counts; Detect incomplete payments (payment_total_value < items total)

accepted.name: order_items_by_product
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  COUNT(*) AS items_sold_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(price,0.0)) AS revenue_price_sum,
  SUM(COALESCE(freight_value,0.0)) AS revenue_freight_sum,
  SUM(COALESCE(price,0.0) + COALESCE(freight_value,0.0)) AS revenue_total_value
FROM order_items
GROUP BY product_id
accepted.description: Aggregate item-level metrics grouped by product: number of times sold, total revenue (price), total freight and total item value. Use for product performance and top-seller analyses. | Use for: Top-selling products by units or revenue; Revenue contribution by product; Join with product attributes for category-level reporting

accepted.name: orders_with_payments_items
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  oi.items_count,
  oi.items_price_sum,
  oi.items_freight_sum,
  oi.items_total_value,
  p.payment_attempts_count,
  p.payment_total_value
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    order_id,
    COUNT(*) AS items_count,
    SUM(COALESCE(price,0.0)) AS items_price_sum,
    SUM(COALESCE(freight_value,0.0)) AS items_freight_sum,
    SUM(COALESCE(price,0.0) + COALESCE(freight_value,0.0)) AS items_total_value
  FROM order_items
  GROUP BY order_id
) oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    order_id,
    COUNT(*) AS payment_attempts_count,
    SUM(COALESCE(payment_value,0.0)) AS payment_total_value
  FROM order_payments
  GROUP BY order_id
) p ON o.order_id = p.order_id
accepted.description: Denormalized order-level view joining orders, aggregated payments, and aggregated order items sums. Use when you need a single row per order with totals from items and payments for reconciliation or order-level analytics. | Use for: Find orders with mismatched payment vs items totals; Compute average order value and payment coverage; Filter orders by totals for downstream cohorting

accepted.name: product_catalog_with_translation
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.product_id,
  p.product_category_name,
  t.product_category_name_english,
  p.product_name_lenght,
  p.product_description_lenght,
  p.product_photos_qty,
  p.product_weight_g,
  p.product_length_cm,
  p.product_height_cm,
  p.product_width_cm
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN product_category_name_translation t
  ON p.product_category_name = t.product_category_name
accepted.description: Product dimension enriched with category translation (English). Use when reporting product attributes with human-readable category labels. | Use for: Report product attributes with translated category labels; Group product-level metrics by English category; Filter products by size/weight thresholds

accepted.name: customer_latest_order_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  customer_id,
  order_purchase_timestamp,
  order_status,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_purchase_timestamp DESC) AS order_rank_per_customer
FROM orders
accepted.description: Rank orders per customer by purchase timestamp (most recent first) and expose row_rank so downstream queries can select latest N orders per customer. | Use for: Select the most recent order(s) per customer; Compute customer recency metrics; Build retention/leaky-bucket cohorts by last N orders

accepted.name: seller_performance_by_order
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  seller_id,
  COUNT(*) AS items_sold_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(price,0.0)) AS seller_price_sum,
  SUM(COALESCE(freight_value,0.0)) AS seller_freight_sum,
  SUM(COALESCE(price,0.0) + COALESCE(freight_value,0.0)) AS seller_total_value,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE (SUM(COALESCE(price,0.0) + COALESCE(freight_value,0.0)) / COUNT(*)) END AS seller_avg_item_value
FROM order_items
GROUP BY seller_id
accepted.description: Aggregate order item metrics by seller: items sold, revenue and average item value. Useful for seller ranking and performance monitoring. | Use for: Rank sellers by revenue or average item value; Identify underperforming sellers with low sales; Combine with sellers table for geographic performance

accepted.name: geolocation_zip_centroids
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
  AVG(geolocation_lat) AS geolocation_lat,
  AVG(geolocation_lng) AS geolocation_lng,
  MIN(geolocation_city) AS geolocation_city,
  MIN(geolocation_state) AS geolocation_state,
  COUNT(*) AS geolocation_points_count
FROM geolocation
GROUP BY geolocation_zip_code_prefix
accepted.description: Compute a representative latitude/longitude per geolocation_zip_code_prefix by averaging points. Use when joining customers/sellers by zip prefix to get approximate centroid coordinates. | Use for: Map customers/sellers by zip prefix centroid; Compute distances between zip centroids; Aggregate regional metrics by zip prefix

accepted.name: orders_with_customer_location
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  c.customer_unique_id,
  c.customer_zip_code_prefix,
  c.customer_city,
  c.customer_state,
  g.geolocation_lat,
  g.geolocation_lng
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT geolocation_zip_code_prefix, AVG(geolocation_lat) AS geolocation_lat, AVG(geolocation_lng) AS geolocation_lng
  FROM geolocation
  GROUP BY geolocation_zip_code_prefix
) g ON c.customer_zip_code_prefix = g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix
accepted.description: Join orders to customer attributes and customer zip centroid (if available). Use for geographic analysis of orders at the customer level. | Use for: Analyze geographic distribution of orders; Segment orders by customer city/state or proximity; Join order-level metrics with location for mapping
